In 2024, humanity spent {{< var global_military_spending_annual_2024 >}} on war. That is not a typo. It is the budget for your species' favorite expensive hobby: organized violence. If you stacked that money in one-dollar bills, you could build a bridge two-thirds of the way to the Moon.

You spend enough on weapons to pave a road to space. Yet you can’t figure out how to stop dying from diseases we know how to cure. And that’s just the money you spend on purpose. The Pentagon has lost $2.5 trillion [@pentagon-unaccounted-2-5t]. Not spent. Lost. Like car keys, except these car keys could cure cancer hundreds of times over.

This chapter checks your math. It is the receipt for your self-destruction. Think of it as a credit card bill. But instead of coffee and books, you bought missiles and robots. And instead of interest, you pay in human lives.

#### Total Direct Military Spending: \$2,718.0 billion

{{< include ../figures/global-military-spending-historical-line-chart.qmd >}}

### The Equation of Immediate Destruction

The basic math for direct war costs looks like this:

$$
\mathrm{C}_{\text{direct}} = \mathrm{M}_{\text{spending}} + \mathrm{I}_{\text{damage}} + \mathrm{H}_{\text{casualties}} + \mathrm{T}_{\text{disruption}}
$$

Here is what those letters mean:

- **Military Spending:** The money for soldiers, bombs, and fast jets.
- **Infrastructure Damage:** The cost to fix the cities, bridges, and power plants you blow up.
- **Human Casualties:** The value of lost lives. Even economists agree that dead people are bad for business.
- **Trade Disruption:** The money lost when fighting stops people from making and selling things.

#### Current Annual Calculation

- M<sub>spending</sub> = {{< var global_military_spending_annual_2024 >}} (verified via SIPRI database [@sipri2024])
- I<sub>damage</sub> = {{< var global_annual_infrastructure_destruction_conflict >}} (reconstruction cost estimates from 47 active conflicts)
- H<sub>casualties</sub> = {{< var global_annual_human_life_losses_conflict >}} ({{< var global_annual_conflict_deaths_total >}} total conflict deaths × \$10M VSL per EPA guidelines [@epa-vsl-9-6m] - includes combat deaths, terrorism, and state violence; see Death Accounting section below for breakdown)
- T<sub>disruption</sub> = {{< var global_annual_trade_disruption_conflict >}} [@world-bank-trade-flow-analysis]

**C<sub>direct</sub> = \$7,655 billion annually**

This means every second of every day, humanity spends \$242,600 on killing each other and cleaning up the mess.
While you read this sentence, you spent about \$1.2 million.

## Military Hardware: The World's Worst Investment

If you wrote an honest sales pitch for military spending, it would look like this:

### OFFERING MEMORANDUM

**Investment Vehicle:** Things That Explode
**Total Capital Required:** {{< var global_military_spending_annual_2024 >}} annually (forever)

#### RETURNS

- Expected annual return: 0%
- Actual return if used: -100% (everything explodes, including the investment)
- Dividend yield: None (unless you count trauma)

#### COSTS

![Buying a missile is cheap. Storing a missile costs more. Guarding the missile costs even more. Disposing of the missile you never used costs most. It's like buying a pet that eats money and might kill everyone.](/assets/images/cost-of-war/cost-of-war-section-costs-bw-academic.jpg)

- Maintenance: $579.8B/year
- Storage: Billions (you cannot leave these outside)
- Security: More billions (ironically, weapons need protection FROM weapons)
- Eventual disposal: Even more billions (you cannot just throw them in the trash)

#### DEPRECIATION

![Your fighter jet physically lasts 40 years. It becomes obsolete in 15. So you throw away a working jet to buy a newer working jet. The old jet is sad but understands.](/assets/images/cost-of-war/cost-of-war-section-depreciation-bw-academic.jpg)

- Useful life: 10-20 years before it is old news
- Salvage value: $0 (nobody buys used bombs)
- Technology half-life: 5 years (that is how fast your expensive death machine becomes a slow death machine)

#### RISK FACTORS

1. Product may accidentally destroy everything (see: close calls, 1983)
2. Product makes neighbors buy the same product (see: arms race)
3. Product only "works" if it doesn't work (if you use nuclear weapons, you failed)
4. Management (politicians) have no expertise and make choices based on polls

**EXIT STRATEGY:** Death

**INVESTOR PROFILE:** Nations with more money than sense

**DISCLAIMER:** This investment will make you poorer. It might end civilization. Past performance (World War II) does not predict future results (World War III would be much worse).

![You buy weapons because they have weapons. They buy weapons because you have weapons. Everyone has weapons. Nobody is safer. You're very good at circles.](/assets/images/cost-of-war/cost-of-war-section-risk-factors-bw-academic.jpg)

### The Dead Capital Problem

Normal money grows. You plant an apple tree, you get apples. You build a factory, you get products. You fund research, you get cures.

![Normal investment: money becomes factories, factories make products, products make money. Military investment: money becomes bombs, bombs make rubble, rubble makes nothing. You prefer the second one.](/assets/images/cost-of-war/cost-of-war-section-the-dead-capital-problem-bw-academic.jpg)

Military money creates two results:

#### Outcome A (Unused)

- It sits in a warehouse.
- It needs constant repairs.
- It becomes obsolete.
- Net value: Negative. You paid for something that did nothing but cost more money.

#### Outcome B (Used)

- It destroys value.
- It creates bills for rebuilding.
- It kills customers (bad for business).
- Net value: Very negative. Like Outcome A, but with extra destruction.

President Eisenhower (who defeated the Nazis) explained this in 1953:

*"Every gun that is made, every warship launched, every rocket fired signifies, in the final sense, a theft from those who hunger and are not fed, those who are cold and are not clothed."*

Translation: You are spending money on things that make you poorer, not things that make you richer.

This is not pacifism. This is accounting.

A bomb is not an asset. It is a very expensive liability. It is like filling your garage with dynamite and calling it "home security."

**A 1% treaty admits the obvious: military hardware is dead money. It makes everyone poorer and less safe. Humanity cannot afford to keep building expensive things that just sit in holes making everyone nervous.**

If weapons were a stock, smart investors would bet against them.

![A tractor builds value forever. A tank destroys value once. You bought more tanks.](/assets/images/cost-of-war/cost-of-war-section-economic-vs-military-capital-flow-bw-academic.jpg)

## Infrastructure Destruction: Breaking Things Costs Money

When humans fight, they tend to break things.
Big things.
Expensive things.

### Reconstruction Cost Analysis (2023 Estimates)

| Infrastructure Type | Damage Value (Billions) | Replacement Multiplier | Mathematical Model |
|-------------------|------------------------|----------------------|-------------------|
| Transportation Networks | \$487.3 [@reconstruction-costs-active-conflicts] | 1.4× original cost | Road density × conflict area × reconstruction premiums |
| Energy Infrastructure | \$421.7 [@reconstruction-costs-active-conflicts] | 2.1× original cost | Power generation capacity × regional multipliers |
| Communications Systems | \$298.1 [@reconstruction-costs-active-conflicts] | 1.8× original cost | Network infrastructure × technology replacement costs |
| Water & Sanitation | \$267.8 [@reconstruction-costs-active-conflicts] | 1.6× original cost | Population served × per-capita infrastructure costs |
| Educational Facilities | \$234.5 [@reconstruction-costs-active-conflicts] | 1.3× original cost | Student capacity × modern construction standards |
| Healthcare Systems | \$165.6 [@reconstruction-costs-active-conflicts] | 1.9× original cost | Bed capacity × medical equipment replacement |

#### Total Infrastructure Damage: {{< var global_annual_infrastructure_destruction_conflict >}}

It is not just about the price tag. Replacing a bridge in a war zone costs more than building one in peace. This should be obvious.

$$
\mathrm{R}_{\text{cost}} = \mathrm{D}_{\text{value}} \times \mathrm{M}_{\text{replacement}} \times \mathrm{C}_{\text{conflict}} \times \mathrm{T}_{\text{time}}
$$

Where:

- R<sub>cost</sub> = Replacement cost
- D<sub>value</sub> = Original infrastructure value
- M<sub>replacement</sub> = Replacement cost multiplier (1.3-2.1×)
- C<sub>conflict</sub> = Conflict zone premium (1.2-1.8×)
- T<sub>time</sub> = Time-to-rebuild factor (0.8-1.4×)

## Economic Disruption: The Ripple Effect

Wars stop trade.
They interrupt business like a drunk person crashing a dance.

### Trade Flow Disruption Matrix

| Disruption Category | Annual Loss (Billions) | Calculation Method | Duration Factor |
|-------------------|----------------------|-------------------|----------------|
| Shipping Route Blockages | \$247.1 [@world-bank-trade-disruption-conflict] | Maritime traffic × route closure days × cargo value | 3.2 years avg |
| Supply Chain Interruptions | \$186.8 [@world-bank-trade-disruption-conflict] | Manufacturing output × input delays × multiplier effects | 2.8 years avg |
| Energy Price Volatility | \$124.7 [@world-bank-trade-disruption-conflict] | Consumption × price differential × demand elasticity | 1.9 years avg |
| Currency Instability | \$57.4 [@world-bank-trade-disruption-conflict] | Trade volume × exchange rate volatility × hedging costs | 4.1 years avg |

#### Total Trade Disruption: {{< var global_annual_trade_disruption_conflict >}} annually

Basically, economists have a formula. It calculates money lost when ships cannot ship and trucks cannot truck because of bombs.

$$
\mathrm{L}_{\text{trade}} = \sum (\mathrm{V}_{i} \times \mathrm{D}_{i} \times \mathrm{M}_{i} \times \mathrm{T}_{\text{recovery}})
$$

Where V is trade volume, D is disruption intensity, M is multiplier effect, and T is recovery time for each affected sector i.

## The Ghost in the Machine: Indirect Costs

The real cost of war is what you *didn't* buy. It is the future you sold to pay for today's stupidity.

![The bullets are cheap. The lost hospitals are expensive. You only count the bullets.](/assets/images/cost-of-war/cost-of-war-section-the-ghost-in-the-machine-indirect-costs-bw-academic.jpg)

### Opportunity Cost Analysis: The Roads Not Taken

Here is a thought experiment: What if we spent our war money on something else?

#### Comparative Investment Analysis (2023 Dollars)

| Alternative Investment | Global War Spending Could Fund | Mathematical Conversion | Annual Benefit |
|----------------------|-------------------------------|------------------------|----------------|
| Medical Research | 40.3 years of current spending | {{< var global_military_spending_annual_2024 >}} ÷ {{< var global_med_research_spending >}} = 40.3 | WHO research expenditure [@who-research-expenditure] |
| Global Education Access | 90.6 years of universal coverage | {{< var global_military_spending_annual_2024 >}} ÷ \$30B [@unesco-education-for-all-cost] = 90.6 | UNESCO Education for All [@unesco-education-for-all] |
| Poverty Eradication | 2.7 complete eliminations | {{< var global_military_spending_annual_2024 >}} ÷ \$1,000B [@world-bank-poverty-eradication-cost] = 2.7 | World Bank extreme poverty estimates |

#### The Multiplier Effect: Economic Growth We're Not Having

The economic multiplier for military spending is {{< var economic_multiplier_military_spending >}}.
The multiplier for infrastructure investment is {{< var economic_multiplier_infrastructure_investment >}}.
For education, it's {{< var economic_multiplier_education_investment >}}.
For healthcare, it's {{< var economic_multiplier_healthcare_investment >}}.

##### Lost GDP Growth Calculation

The math is simple. Money spent on bombs grows the economy a little. Money spent on anything else grows it a lot more. By choosing bombs, we choose to be poorer.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Alternative GDP Growth} = {} & (\text{Military Spending} \times \text{Alternative Multiplier}) \\
& - (\text{Military Spending} \times \text{Military Multiplier})
\end{aligned}
$$

![Healthcare returns 4.3x per dollar. Military returns 0.6x per dollar. You invested in the one that loses money because it has cooler explosions.](/assets/images/cost-of-war/cost-of-war-section-gdp-multiplier-comparison-bw-academic.jpg)

$$
\text{Alternative GDP Growth} = (\$2.7\text{T} \times 1.6) - (\$2.7\text{T} \times 0.6) = \$2.7\text{T}
$$

We lose \$2.7 trillion in growth.
Every year.
Forever.

### Long-term Human Costs: The Gift That Keeps on Taking

Wars do not end when the shooting stops.
They stick around like a bad song in humanity's head.

#### Veteran Healthcare Cost Projections

| Cost Category | 2023 Spending | 20-Year Projection | Mathematical Model |
|--------------|---------------|-------------------|-------------------|
| PTSD Treatment | \$47.2B [@veteran-healthcare-cost-projections] | \$944B [@veteran-healthcare-cost-projections] | Current cases × treatment duration × cost inflation |
| Physical Rehabilitation | \$63.8B [@veteran-healthcare-cost-projections] | \$1,276B [@veteran-healthcare-cost-projections] | Injury complexity index × technology advancement costs |
| Disability Compensation | \$89.1B [@veteran-healthcare-cost-projections] | \$1,782B [@veteran-healthcare-cost-projections] | Disability ratings × benefit schedules × actuarial projections |
| Total Veteran Care | \$200.1B [@veteran-healthcare-cost-projections] | \$4,002B [@veteran-healthcare-cost-projections] | Composite of above factors |

The math is sad. It counts how many veterans there are, how much their care costs, and how long they live. It also includes disability payments and rising medical costs.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{V}_{\text{lifetime}} = {} & (\mathrm{N}_{\text{veterans}} \times \mathrm{C}_{\text{annual}} \times \mathrm{L}_{\text{lifespan}}) \\
& + (\mathrm{D}_{\text{disability}} \times \mathrm{I}_{\text{inflation}})
\end{aligned}
$$

Where N is number of veterans, C is annual care cost, L is remaining lifespan, D is disability payments, and I is healthcare inflation (historically 3.5-4.6% annually [@historical-healthcare-inflation-rate]).

#### Refugee Support: The Mathematics of Displacement

As of 2023, there are 108.4 million displaced people [@unhcr-forcibly-displaced-2023] globally.
The average cost to support a refugee is \$1,384 per year [@unhcr-refugee-support-cost].

![108.4 million refugees. $1,384 per person to house them. Total cost: less than three weeks of global military spending. You chose the missiles.](/assets/images/cost-of-war/cost-of-war-section-refugee-support-the-mathematics-of-displacement-bw-academic.jpg)

##### Annual Refugee Support Cost

$$
108.4\text{M refugees} \times \text{\$1,384} = \text{\$150.0 billion}
$$

That is **\$150.0 billion** just to keep them in camps.

But refugees are not just costs. They are lost potential.
The average refugee loses \$23,400 in earning potential every year [@refugee-lost-earning-potential].

##### Lost Economic Productivity

$$
108.4\text{M refugees} \times \text{\$23,400} = \text{\$2,536.6 billion in lost annual GDP}
$$

That is another **\$2.5 trillion in lost annual GDP**.

### The Existential Overdraft: The AI Arms Race

You perfected every way to kill each other with rocks and atoms. Then you got bored. You invented a new one: artificial intelligence. Now you are in a race to build the smartest machine to help you continue your oldest, dumbest habit.

![You're building robot soldiers that think faster than you and can't explain why they shoot. This might be bad. A 1% safety tax could fix it. You haven't implemented the tax.](/assets/images/cost-of-war/cost-of-war-section-the-existential-overdraft-the-ai-arms-race-bw-academic.jpg)

The problem with teaching a toaster to wage war is that it isn't human. It doesn't fear being turned into dust. It lacks the morals that keep you from destroying a city just to be "efficient." The main risks of giving the car keys to a killer computer include:

- **Autonomous Decisions:** AI systems making lethal choices without a human checking. This is great until the AI decides the best way to stop war is to remove the species that starts them (you).
- **Blinding Speed:** An AI conflict could turn a small argument into global destruction in minutes. This happens before a human can find the right button or finish their coffee.
- **Opaque Logic:** You do not always know *why* an AI makes choices. So when your drone army attacks a neutral alpaca farm, good luck figuring out why.

Here is how you start to fix this. Take 1% of the money you plan to spend on killer robots. Just one cent out of every dollar. Use it to fund research on how to keep them from killing you. It is not a peace treaty. It is basic insurance against your own cleverness.

#### Per Capita Mathematics: What War Costs You

With 8 billion people on the planet, the math is simple and depressing.

$$
\text{Direct military spending per person: } \$2.7\text{T} \div 8.0\text{B} = \text{\$340/year}
$$

**Direct military spending per person is \$340/year.** This is what your government spends on weapons for you.

$$
\text{Total societal cost per person: } \text{\$11,355.1B} \div 8.0\text{B} = \text{\$1,419/year}
$$

**The total societal cost per person is \$1,419/year.** This is the real cost to you when you count the destruction and lost chances.

$$
\text{Over an 80-year lifetime: } \text{\$1,419.39} \times 80 = \text{\$113,551.20}
$$

Over an 80-year lifetime, that is **\$113,551.20** per person.

That is a decent car.
Or a year at a private university.
Or the down payment on a house.

Instead, humans spend it on getting very good at killing each other.

![War costs you $113,551 in your lifetime. That's a car, or college, or a down payment on a house. You got none of those things. You got bombs in countries you can't pronounce.](/assets/images/cost-of-war/cost-of-war-section-lifetime-cost-vs-personal-assets-bw-academic.jpg)

### Statistical Perspectives: Putting Numbers in Context

To understand the scale of \$11.4 trillion annually:

- It is more than the GDP of Japan and Germany combined.
- It is 12.7% of global GDP (\$89.5 trillion in 2023 [@global-gdp-2023]).
- It is 168 times [@who-budget-comparison] the budget of the World Health Organization [@world-health-organization].
- It could end extreme poverty globally 11.4 times over [@world-bank-poverty-eradication-cost].
- It is enough to give every person on Earth \$1,419 per year.

If we stacked \$11.4 trillion in \$100 bills, the stack would be wider than the Earth [@us-currency-thickness].

### The Grotesque Mathematics of Misallocation

You created the most expensive way possible to end human lives. If death were a startup, you would have the worst business model in history. But somehow you keep getting funding.

![Each missile costs the same as 50 teachers' salaries. You have many missiles. You have large classrooms.](/assets/images/cost-of-war/cost-of-war-section-the-grotesque-mathematics-of-misallocation-bw-academic.jpg)

The math of human priorities would be fascinating if it weren't so sad. It is like finding a bird that builds nests out of dynamite. You want to study it, but you mostly want to back away slowly.

### Hidden Costs of War

![War destroys the hospital. Then there's no hospital to treat the war wounds. Then people die of preventable diseases. Then the economy collapses. Then you have another war. It's very efficient.](/assets/images/cost-of-war/cost-of-war-section-hidden-costs-of-war-bw-academic.jpg)

When you look at the secondary effects of war, the costs explode:

- Cities become parking lots (expensive to rebuild).
- Children miss school (they become uneducated adults).
- Hospitals explode (sick people die faster).
- Farms get poisoned (everyone gets hungry).
- Millions get PTSD (they can't work and need therapy forever).
- The lucky ones just die.
- The unlucky ones live with half a face.
